 Detailed Forecast
 Synopsis
 Breezy to locally strong gusty trade winds will occur through Saturday. Quick passing showers caught up within this trade flow will primarily focus along windward and upslope mauka areas. Upper ridging will nose in from the west and, along with a drier air mass settling in over the Central Pacific, assist in producing a few drier days to begin Thanksgiving Week.
 Discussion
 The state sits in a height weakness region between two upper ridges centered west of the International Dateline and the other over the eastern Pacific. This weak col in the height field has been just enough to destabilize the regional atmosphere in recent days resulting in mostly cloudy days and more frequent showers. A large 1035 mb surface high about 1,300 nm north-northwest of the islands in pressing down a tight enough pressure gradient across the region to maintain breezy to locally strong trade winds today and tomorrow. A slightly less stable atmosphere, along with the southern passage of a couple of weak ribbons of higher PVA, will create a slightly elevated inversion/deeper boundary layer. A deeper boundary layer lends itself to sub-Wind Advisory 20 to 30 mph gusts to 40 mph winds within the windiest spots such as along upper terrain ridgelines and through steep valleys. Water vapor and 12Z soundings are evidence that a drier air mass will be working its way in from the east the next couple of days. There will still be enough lower level moisture trapped up within shortwave energy to produce the typical trade shower behavior over the usual suspect windward and upslope mauka areas through tomorrow…more frequent periods of light precipitation occurring at night. Most leeward areas will remain dry with occasionally better organized showers making their way overtop Oahu's Wai'anae or Koolau range or mid day shower development across Big Island's Kona slopes during peak warming.
Western Pacific ridging begins to slowly advance east over the weekend while blocking and steering away eastern-passing weak northern Pacific troughs. Increasing heights will increase stability, along with drier mid layer air working into the lower layers in response to the mid level ridging/subsidence going into the holiday weekend. The first few days of the week look pretty nice with more sun and very infrequent shower activity being confined to the upper terrain. This western-based ridging never truly establishes itself over Hawaii, preferring to stay out west and allow weak troughs to skirt just east of the state Monday and Thursday. Monday's boundary will be too weak and north of the islands to be of any notice but Thursday's trough will dig further south and increase rain chances from northwest to southeast Thanksgiving Day with the approach of the associated cold front. This series of weak trough passages will disrupt the early week upstream pressure gradient just enough to produce light easterly to variable breezes by early Wednesday. A front will likely pass across the island chain Thanksgiving Day with strengthened north northeast winds in its wake that afternoon into evening. The state falls under a similar synoptic pattern of a lower height field between two ridges by next weekend. Breezy winds will veer easterly under partly cloudy skies with low rain chances this time next week per a slowly modifying post-frontal air mass.
 Aviation
 Breezy trade winds will usher in scattered showers somewhat enhanced by an upper trough building over the area. Higher coverage of clouds and showers expected tonight into Saturday as an old frontal band is pushed in by the trade wind flow.
AIRMET Sierra is posted for tempo mountain obscurations above 2000 feet across windward sides of Kauai, Oahu, Molokai, Maui and windward/southeast Big Island. This AIRMET is likely to continue through the rest of this morning.
AIRMET Tango is posted for leeward sections of all islands below 7000 feet due to the breezy trade winds, which is expected to continue over the next couple of days. Anticipate AIRMET Tango remaining in effect at least through the end of today.
 Marine
 Fresh to locally strong trade will continue today. A Small Craft Advisory (SCA) remains in effect for all waters through tonight. Winds look to decrease later in the weekend and could become light by early next week as the subtropical ridge sinks south over the islands. By the middle of next week, NW winds look to ramp up quickly with the potential passing of a cold front. This frontal passage could also have XL swell assoicated with it.
For north facing shores, small surf is expected today. Another small north- northwest swell is forecast to arrive and build on Saturday, peaking Saturday night into Sunday, with a larger (advisory level) and longer lived northwest swell expected next Tuesday. A potential XL northwest swell is then possible by the middle of next week as models indicate a strong storm force low developing far north of the islands next week. However, model discrepancies over the strength and position of the fetch are notable at this time, so the size of the swell is still a bit uncertain. It also looks more likely that any large swell will be accompanied by strong NW or N winds.
Rough surf along east-facing shores expected as the trades stregthen today. A small, long- period swell will bring a bump to south shore surf today, and could keep south shore surf slightly elevated through the weekend.
 Fire weather
 Breezy to locally strong trades are expected today. Showers riding in on the trades should maintain near normal humidities. These conditions will make for a low to moderate fire weather threat this afternoon. An extended period of drier weather returns much of next week. Weak shortwave energy passing over the region will create slightly higher afternoon temperature inversion heights between 7,000 to 8,000 feet.
 HFO Watches/Warnings/Advisories
 Small Craft Advisory until 6 PM HST this evening for Alenuihaha Channel, Big Island Leeward Waters, Big Island Southeast Waters, Big Island Windward Waters, Kaiwi Channel, Kauai Channel, Kauai Leeward Waters, Kauai Northwest Waters, Kauai Windward Waters, Maalaea Bay, Maui County Leeward Waters, Maui County Windward Waters, Oahu Leeward Waters, Oahu Windward Waters, Pailolo Channel.
